items.title: Named owner and consumer seams are absent from dependency metadata
items.statement: LSPS-042 names an SSH-owner consumer boundary, but its dependency list is empty; the same empty dependency and unblock fields recur across the reviewed PlanUnits even when canonical text names FileManager, SSH, Search, Source Control, Problems, buffers, and diffs. The window therefore does not encode ordering, caller, or consumer obligations in machine-addressable dependency metadata.
items.impact: Compilation or implementation can schedule LSP behavior without the owner contracts and downstream consumers that must agree on it.
items.builder_discretion: The graph representation is discretionary, but the required owner and consumer edges are not.

evidence.exact_quote: - Settings > SSH and GUI remote-editor surfaces consume the SSH owner contract instead of redefining it.

items.title: Remote path mapping has no normalization or adversarial-input contract
items.statement: The prohibition on hidden mirrors, retargeting, and URI collisions does not define validation and canonicalization for dot segments, symlinks, case differences, URI escaping, malformed identities, or paths outside the authorized remote root.
items.impact: Equivalent or hostile path spellings can bypass root authority, collide, or bind a document to the wrong server session.
items.builder_discretion: Normalization mechanics may vary, but accepted inputs, rejection behavior, and root-containment invariants require a contract.

evidence.exact_quote: - Puppet Master must not create a hidden local mirror, silently retarget multi-context work to local host, or let host-local URI collisions occur.

items.title: Identity changes lack an explicit transition and invalidation policy
items.statement: LSPS-041 preserves live host/server/root keys and forbids silent retargeting, but does not specify what happens to open documents, outstanding requests, diagnostics, caches, or pending edits when the SSH profile, host identity, mapping, root, or server identity changes.
items.impact: Old-context results can be applied after an authority change or users can be stranded without a defined reject, detach, migrate, or reconnect transition.
items.builder_discretion: The chosen transition UX may vary; invalidation, cancellation, and explicit user authority cannot remain implicit.

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Remote LSP identity preserves user-visible SSH authority, remote-host and working-folder path authority, host-scoped path mapping, and live host/server/root session keys while forbidding hidden mirrors, silent multi-context retargeting, and local-only session-key collisions.

items.title: Validated-cache and offline-edit semantics are undefined
items.statement: The degraded UX permits offline work when a validated cache exists, but does not define validation authority, freshness or expiry, which operations are allowed, how offline edits are journaled, how reconnect conflicts are surfaced, or when cached diagnostics cease to be truthful.
items.impact: Users can edit or trust stale state under a reassuring offline label and later face silent overwrite, duplicate mutation, or unresolvable synchronization conflicts.
items.builder_discretion: Cache technology is discretionary; freshness, permitted actions, conflict states, and reconnect reconciliation are product contracts.

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Remote LSP degraded and connection-loss states follow FileManager and SSH owner patterns by showing Connection lost, Reconnect, Work offline when a validated cache exists, system keychain/agent credential handling, Settings > SSH capability/degraded copy, and shared read-only/offline vocabulary.

items.title: Credential and remote-host trust lifecycle is not specified
items.statement: System keychain or agent handling is named, but the window does not define host-key verification, profile replacement, credential revocation, prompt cancellation, agent disappearance, or whether secrets and authentication errors may enter projections, logs, caches, or user-visible copy.
items.impact: Connection recovery can authenticate the wrong host, leak credential-adjacent data, or repeatedly prompt without a deterministic terminal state.
items.builder_discretion: Platform integration details may vary; trust prompts, revocation, cancellation, and secret-redaction boundaries require explicit behavior.

items.title: Previewed workspace mutations lack versioning, atomicity, and rollback
items.statement: Preview confirmation and per-file failure reports are explicit, but there is no precondition that files remain at the previewed versions, no definition of atomic versus best-effort apply, and no rollback or retry rule after a subset succeeds.
items.impact: A rename, broad format, or code action can apply to changed content or leave a workspace internally inconsistent while only reporting the damage after the fact.
items.builder_discretion: Transaction mechanics may vary, but stale-preview detection, outcome semantics, and recovery obligations must be fixed.

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: 'Remote LSP mutation and outage modes remain visible and FileSafe-gated: rename, broad format, and multi-file code actions require preview confirmation; partial failures report per-file results; remote modes disclose full, diagnostics-only, or no-LSP state; adjacent Search, Source Control, Problems, buffers, and diffs do not silently fall back.'
- partial workspace-edit failure reports per-file results

items.title: Degraded-mode propagation has labels but no transition oracle
items.statement: The three remote modes and stale or pending-sync tokens are preserved, yet the window does not define the events that enter and leave each mode, whether states are per document or session, which actions each surface disables, or how all named consumers converge on the same generation of state.
items.impact: Editor, Problems, Search, Source Control, buffers, and diffs can simultaneously present conflicting availability or stale data without technically performing a silent fallback.
items.builder_discretion: Visual styling is discretionary; state-entry criteria, capability gating, and propagation consistency are not.

items.title: Compatibility cleanup has no migration or residue-detection rule
items.statement: LSPS-044 assigns browser-panel and preview_mode tokens outside LSPSupport, but does not say how persisted sessions, older configuration, generated artifacts, or restored state containing those tokens are detected, migrated, rejected, or proven absent.
items.impact: Legacy state can reintroduce the forbidden vocabulary or silently lose recovery and preview behavior during upgrade.
items.builder_discretion: Migration implementation may vary; accepted legacy inputs and terminal dispositions require a contract.

evidence.exact_quote: - Browser-panel and preview_mode tokens are compatibility cleanup residue owned outside LSPSupport.

items.title: Module layout omits runtime ownership and target-compatibility boundaries
items.statement: The crate and file layout fixes dependencies but does not define who owns the Tokio runtime, task cancellation and shutdown, bounded channels, blocking work, feature gating, or behavior on targets where process-spawn and networking capabilities differ.
items.impact: A conforming layout can still leak tasks, deadlock shutdown, exhaust queues, or fail to compile or degrade predictably on a supported target.
items.builder_discretion: Internal APIs remain discretionary, but runtime lifecycle, backpressure, and supported-target behavior should be explicit.

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: The LSP client and registry live in the same crate as the editor under a dedicated src/lsp module with client, registry, session/server_handle, document/sync files and lsp-types plus tokio dependencies, while tower-lsp is unnecessary unless implementing a server.

items.title: Projection fields have no invariants or coherent-update contract
items.statement: LSPS-046 lists keys and projection fields without defining enum domains, uniqueness, nullability, precedence between requested_enabled and effective_enabled, version monotonicity, attached-server ordering or deduplication, or atomic snapshot semantics when lifecycle, health, capability, and document bindings update concurrently.
items.impact: Consumers can observe impossible combinations, route a document through duplicate or stale servers, or overwrite a newer binding with an older projection.
items.builder_discretion: Data structures may vary; validity invariants and publication ordering require a single contract.

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Core LSP conceptual structures preserve LspSessionKey, LspSessionProjection, and DocumentBinding fields for project, host, server, root, lifecycle, freshness, health, enablement, capability, restart, error, path, version, and attached server identity.

items.title: Projection privacy, retention, and support diagnostics are unspecified
items.statement: Root identity, path, and last_error are projected fields, but the window does not define redaction, retention, persistence, telemetry eligibility, support-bundle inclusion, user deletion, or correlation timestamps and request identifiers.
items.impact: Remote paths, host identity, source text fragments, or credential-adjacent errors can persist or leave the device, while support cannot reliably reconstruct which session generation produced an error.
items.builder_discretion: Storage format is discretionary; sensitive-field classification, retention, redaction, deletion, and correlation boundaries are not.

items.title: Lifecycle vocabulary and transition graph are internally incomplete
items.statement: The preserved user/state names include ShuttingDown and RestartBackoff, while the transition string uses stopping and crashed; Crashed is not present in the preserved state-name list, and no allowed transition edges, triggering events, terminal conditions, or illegal-transition handling are defined.
items.impact: Implementations and GUI projections can disagree on state identity and permit feature traffic or restart actions during an undefined lifecycle phase.
items.builder_discretion: Internal enum spelling may vary only if a normative mapping and complete transition table exist.

evidence.exact_quote: - stopped → starting → initializing → ready → degraded → stopping → crashed

items.title: Restart and resource limits lack scope, enforcement, and exhaustion behavior
items.statement: The window preserves three attempts, 2s/4s/8s, 512MB, and 30s, but does not define whether limits are per request, server, project, or host; how memory and CPU time are measured; what is cancelled or killed; when the restart budget resets; or what users and pending operations see after exhaustion.
items.impact: Servers can be terminated inconsistently, retry storms can synchronize across sessions, and pending work can disappear or duplicate after forced restart.
items.builder_discretion: Enforcement mechanisms may vary; accounting scope, reset rules, cancellation, terminal state, and user-visible consequences require definition.

items.title: GUI states lack accessibility and localization requirements
items.statement: GUI-related units preserve literal English labels for connection loss and actions, but the reviewed core contains no contract for localized expansion, stable translation keys, screen-reader announcements, focus movement, keyboard reachability, non-color state cues, or reduced-motion behavior during reconnect and degradation.
items.impact: Connection and destructive-action state may be unavailable or misleading to assistive-technology users and can break or become ambiguous in translated interfaces.
items.builder_discretion: Copy styling and translation tooling are discretionary; semantic announcements, operability, and localization-safe state identity are not.

items.title: Acceptance and validation do not falsify runtime behavior
items.statement: Each reviewed PlanUnit repeats source-traceability criteria and plan migration or index validation, but none provides executable or observable oracles for path collision, retarget rejection, cache validity, reconnect, partial workspace mutation, degraded propagation, projection invariants, lifecycle transitions, restart exhaustion, or resource enforcement.
items.impact: Governance checks can pass while every runtime safety and GUI-truth obligation remains untested and mutually inconsistent.
items.builder_discretion: Test framework is discretionary; scenario preconditions, observable outcomes, and failure oracles are required.

evidence.exact_quote: - The covered source span remains losslessly available for exact-text audit.

items.title: High-risk remote mutations require visible preview confirmation
items.statement: The core explicitly requires rename, broad format, and multi-file code actions to use the FileSafe preview and confirmation path, so omission of user confirmation for these named destructive operations is not a gap in this window.

evidence.exact_quote: - Preview-worthy remote mutations require the same safe preview/confirmation path as FileSafe edits.

items.title: Silent local Git fallback is expressly forbidden
items.statement: Remote Source Control may not silently fall back to local Git, so the basic negative authority boundary for this fallback is explicit even though detailed outage-state propagation remains underspecified.

evidence.exact_quote: - Remote Source Control must not silently fall back to local Git.

items.title: Normal feature traffic is gated to Ready
items.statement: LSPS-047 explicitly limits normal feature traffic to Ready and requires reduced capability or recovery status elsewhere, establishing a useful top-level traffic gate despite the incomplete state graph.

evidence.exact_quote: - Only Ready emits normal feature traffic; degraded and restart states expose reduced capability or recovery status.

items.title: Referenced owner documents may define some missing seam behavior
items.statement: The core points to storage, GitHub Integration, FileManager, FinalGUISpec, and SSH owner boundaries, but blind-window rules prohibit reading those documents. It is therefore unknown whether they supply compatible cache, save, credential, GUI-state, or recovery contracts; the missing dependency representation inside this window remains a separately supportable gap.
items.impact: Seam completeness and contradictions cannot be certified from this assignment alone.
items.builder_discretion: No seam should be assumed satisfied until the referenced owners are reviewed in an authorized cross-document phase.

dimension_assessments.summary: Named owner and consumer surfaces are not represented by dependency or unblock metadata.
Identity changes, cache transitions, degraded propagation, projection enablement, and lifecycle states lack complete transition rules.
Preview-to-apply races, incoherent projection publication, and restart or limit races are not constrained.
Per-file reporting is explicit, but atomicity, stale-preview rejection, retry, and subset-success semantics are missing.
Offline reconciliation, workspace-edit rollback, and post-restart pending-operation recovery are undefined.
Owner names and anti-fallback constraints exist, but path authority changes, remote trust, and dependency enforcement remain incomplete.
Projected remote identity, paths, and errors lack retention, redaction, telemetry, and deletion rules.
Remote identity and path inputs lack normalization, containment, and malformed-input behavior.
Offline-cache truth and cross-surface degraded state can be stale or inconsistent despite explicit labels.
Connection-loss labels and offline availability are named, but cache validity, edit journaling, conflicts, and reconnect reconciliation are absent.
Projection cardinality and server resource limits lack scope, accounting, enforcement, and exhaustion behavior.
GUI connection, degraded, and confirmation states have no assistive-technology or keyboard contract.
Literal English state labels lack localization keys, expansion constraints, and semantic mapping requirements.
Compatibility residue, persisted projections, schema evolution, and differing runtime targets lack migration behavior.
Per-file outcomes and last_error exist, but correlation, timing, redaction, restart evidence, and support-bundle rules are absent.
Preview confirmation is an explicit non-gap, while stale-preview, partial-apply, and rollback semantics remain safety gaps.
This window omits dependency encoding for named owners; whether referenced documents close the semantic seams is unknown under blind rules.
Validation is limited to migration and index structure, with no runtime or GUI behavioral oracles.
Authorized evidence cannot establish whether referenced owner documents close or contradict the identified seams.
